data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"A decentralized network is more resilient to correlated failure than a redundant monolith because it leverages 'operational heterogeneity' as a primary firewall against systemic software bugs.","counterconditions":[{"case":"The decentralized network adopts a standardized 'best-practice' substrate (e.g., a single managed Kubernetes provider) that re-introduces homogeneity.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"The monolith employs 'N-version programming' or diverse redundancy (different binaries for the same function).","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"The decentralized network's resilience is derived from the variance in its execution environments (different kernels, OS versions, and hardware).
